title: Google DeepMind Releases EmbeddingGemma 2 to Unify Text and Multimedia Embeddings

tickers.name: Alphabet Inc. Class A Common Stock

summary:
The newly released 744M-parameter model from Google DeepMind can process text, code, images, audio, and video into a shared 768-dimensional space. Published alongside its Apache 2.0 weights, EmbeddingGemma 2 eliminates the need for separate encoders or a preliminary transcription step for audio and video inputs.

The model's modular architecture allows users to load specific components, such as the 271M text backbone or 305M audio encoder, reducing peak memory usage on a Pixel 11 Pro to as low as 191 MB for text-only tasks. On the MTEB Code benchmark, the model scored 78.7, an increase from 68.8 for EmbeddingGemma 1, placing it within 2 points of a model 28x its size.

selectedTweets.text:
Want to know how EmbeddingGemma 2 works behind the scenes? The @GoogleDeepMind team published the paper below. My short version:

One 744M model embeds text, code, images, audio and video into a single 768d space. No separate encoders, no transcription step in front.

- Modular: 271M text backbone, 167M vision encoder, 305M audio encoder. Load only what you need. With int4 weights, peak memory on a Pixel 11 Pro is 191 MB text-only and 567 MB full multimodal.
- Simpler per-layer embeddings: it drops the dedicated lookup table and derives them from the main embeddings. Fewer parameters, slightly better scores in their ablation.
- Native audio beats transcribe-then-embed: even 256d audio vectors outperform full-size ASR-based ones.
- Truncation: 768d down to 128d is 6x less vector storage, but audio quality drops sharply at 128d (69.5 to 56.7). 256d holds up much better.
- Code: MTEB Code goes from 68.8 to 78.7 versus EmbeddingGemma 1, within 2 points of a model 28x larger.

Model weights (Apache 2.0): https://t.co/SI1eq4SXsb
